slides.title: The CARFAX moat is real and widening, but growth is now price-led and the margin story keeps resetting

items.title: 1  Growth is mostly price, and new business is fading
items.body: Price was ~$36m of the $64m 6M-26 revenue increase (~4.2pt of 7.5% growth); new business fell from ~$12m (Q1) to ~$8m (Q2). The Form 10/A had called Q1 growth "new business".

items.title: 2  The CARFAX moat is wide and widening; B2B's is moderate
items.body: 177k+ sources and 38bn+ records (records +9.3%/yr since FY16); organic growth beat industry units in 10 of 11 years. B2B grew +3.1% / +5.9% with -18% FY25 flow-through.

items.title: 3  The margin narrative keeps resetting
items.body: SPGI's 41-43% target was missed (39.9% FY25); standalone and one-time costs drifted to the top of their ranges; +50bp/yr expansion now starts in 2028.

items.title: 4  The spin changes earnings power, not cash power
items.body: Interest rises from $13m to ~$110m (~31% of normalized OP). Standalone normalized NI is ~$171m vs $220m carve-out; the dividend is ~41% of it but only ~19% of FCF.

items.title: 5  Disclosure retreated as metrics weakened; pay is loosely tied to performance
items.body: NRR pulled, organic growth no longer printed, segment measure switched the quarter B2B OP fell to $3m. PSUs became time-vested RSUs; no TSR metric; insiders <1%.

items.text: Likeliest loss: a slow de-rating of a ~7% grower with ~39-40% margins and 2.7x gross leverage, not a moat collapse [Inference].
Like-for-like growth has stepped down: ~10% (2015-22) to 8.6% (FY23-25) to ~7% (FY26 guide).
What would change our mind: printed dealer-location, retention and price-per-location KPIs.
